source_ref: Gyurkovics, Stafford & Levita (2020) JEP:General 149(6):1017-1031, doi:10.1037/xge0000698, accepted manuscript https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/152525/ (Method, 'Sustained Attention to Response Task (SART) with thought probes'); OSF https://osf.io/7vbtr/ (sart_merge.csv sha256 cffa74d8..., readme.txt, Gyurkovics_Stafford_Levita_analyses.R sha256 7ded5373...)
note: mapping_basis=reconstructed: probe_01..probe_10 are script-generated integers (data/cogcontrol_gyurkovics.py numbers each participant's code==3 SART trials 1..10 in block/trial order), not source column names. Re-running that construction over the OSF sart_merge.csv reproduces the live table row for row: 1170/1170 (id,item) rows agree on trial_block, trial_num and resp; probes 01-05 fall in block 1 and 06-10 in block 2 for all 117 participants. All ten items carry the same item_text because every probe trial presented the same question; the paper states that on the 10 probe trials 'instead of a digit, participants saw the following probe question until they responded'. text_source=study_materials: item_text and the four option strings are transcribed verbatim from the accepted manuscript's Method, the curly apostrophe in 'wasn’t' kept as printed; the instrument name is IRW's description. RESP AXIS: live resp is the 'overall MW' dichotomy, not the four administered options. The deposit's own analysis script codes key 97 = on-task (p1), 98 = space out (p2), 99 = zone out (p3), 100 = tune out (p4) and mw = 1 for 99/100, matching the paper's printed option order and its definition of overall MW as 'MW with and without awareness ... collapsed'. So resp 0 = 'I was thinking about the task' OR 'My mind was blank', and resp 1 = the zone-out OR the tune-out option. Each resp row's option_text lists both administered options joined with '; ' (the options contain no semicolons). No label for the collapsed categories exists anywhere in the source. Corroborated against published numbers: per-category age-effect Wald chi2 (paper Table 3) reproduce from the live table as 6.924/6.592/0.576/10.286/10.211 vs published 6.92/6.59/0.58/10.29/10.21, and OR early vs late adolescents for overall MW is 0.406 vs published .406 (2.465 with resp flipped). instructions blank: no verbatim instruction screen is published (same call as the sibling _sart/_flanker/_simon tables). English administration (all included participants native English speakers per readme), so no language/_translated columns. RIGHTS: the probe is a research thought-probe (after Jackson & Balota 2012; Smallwood et al. 2007) printed in the paper's Method; no fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause could be found or quoted on the OSF node (no licence stated) or in the manuscript, so nothing blocks.
public_note: Every item in this table is the same thought-probe question, asked 10 times during the SART (probe_01-05 in block 1, probe_06-10 in block 2), and resp collapses its four answer options into two: 0 = on-task or mind blank, 1 = mind drifted without awareness (zone out) or with awareness (tune out), so each option_text lists the two administered options it combines; the four-way report is in the response table's trial_report column.

note: CLEAN PASS WITH CAVEAT (batch_263). 45 rows = 9 items x 5 levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets (9/9 items, resp 1-5). CODE DERIVATION: data/mede_2025_tisp.py melts every ds_main.csv column starting CLIM_EMO_ by name (var_name='item'), so each IRW code IS the source column name (pattern 1, no rename, no positional step); the codes are also self-describing (CLIM_EMO_angry = 'Angry'). MAPPING BASIS data_labels: the core QSF's ChoiceDataExportTags pair each export column with its choice Display text, 9/9 (choice 2 CLIM_EMO_helpless='Helpless', 3 anxious='Anxious', 5 optimistic='Optimistic', 6 angry='Angry', 7 guilty='Guilty', 8 ashamed='Ashamed', 9 depressed='Depressed', 12 pessimistic='Pessimistic', 13 indifferent='Indifferent'), and the master .docx table 46 prints the same 9 words each followed by its code in parentheses, 9/9 identical. Step 5b exempt. Item order shipped is the QSF ChoiceOrder; the QSF sets Randomization Type 'All', so respondents saw the 9 in random order. Inline HTML span styling stripped from Display text; words otherwise verbatim. INSTRUCTIONS: the QSF QuestionText, identical in the .docx: 'To what extent does climate change make you feel any of the following?'. The preceding CLIM_TRUST block carries the section transition 'In the remainder of the survey, we would like to ask you some questions on the topic of climate change.' -- not part of this block, not shipped. OPTIONS: QSF Answers 1='Not at all', 2-4 Display ' ' (blank), 5='Very strongly'; RecodeValues identity 1..5; .docx header 'Not at all (1) | (2) | (3) | (4) | Very strongly (5)'. Options 2-4 shipped blank, not padded. The processing script keeps 1-5 only. Live item x resp counts (server-side GROUP BY) show every item using all 5 levels; per-item n 70,678 (ashamed) to 71,758 (optimistic). Sanity: indifferent is the least endorsed (mean 2.28) vs helpless 3.09 / anxious 3.08, as expected. LANGUAGE: multi-language administration. The paper: 'The core questionnaire was developed in English and was used in countries where English is a widely spoken language. In other countries, the questionnaire was translated into local languages and dialects' -- 36 named (Albanian ... Ukrainian), 37 with English. Shipped the English core questionnaire in the base fields (administered wording for English-language samples), text_source=study_materials, no _translated columns, and language = the semicolon list of all 37 (English first, then the paper's order), per the szameitat_2015_* ruling (Ben, 2026-09-11). UNLIKE the szameitat precedent, the translated wording IS in the deposit: 05_survey-materials/questionnaire/countries/ holds 89 per-sample questionnaire PDFs, and the paper says 'The complete questionnaires in all 37 languages ... are available at OSF'. They were not transcribed because the one-text-per-item schema cannot carry 37 versions in one table; the paper also warns 'a few local questionnaires contained errors' and recommends the core questionnaire for labels and codes. Respondent shares by language are not reliably recoverable from the table: cov_language (Qualtrics UserLanguage) reads EN for 36,080 of 71,910 respondents but has no JA/TR/EL/HU/ID/BN code at all although Japanese, Turkish, Greek, Hungarian, Indonesian and Bengali versions were fielded, so locally programmed translations evidently report EN. Flag for the orchestrator: whether per-language rows should be added later is a schema question, not an extraction one. STEP 3b: matches -- the paper's 'Emotions about climate change' measure: 'nine emotions: helpless; anxious; optimistic; angry; guilty; ashamed; depressed; pessimistic; indifferent (not at all - very strongly)'. RIGHTS: no block. Study-developed items ('Most of the nine items were based on established measures for climate change emotions, such as those developed by Hogg et al. and Searle and Gow'); the shipped wording is nine single emotion words, not a reproduction of either source scale; deposit CC BY 4.0; neither Hogg (HEAS) nor Searle & Gow appears in instrument_rights_register.csv; no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located. section_id trivial; section_prompt and correct_response blank.
